newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban say downed opposition jet.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban say downed opposition jet.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia shot down an opposition jet fighter on Wednesday in the northwestern province of Badghis, a Pakistan-based private Afghan news service said.

The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted a Taleban spokesman in the southern Afghan town Kandahar as saying the jet was one of at least two aircraft belonging to northern Uzbek chief General Abdul Rashid Dostum that heavily bombed Taleban positions on Bala Murghab frontline in northern Badghis.
No further details of the incident were available.

AIP quoted the Taleban spokesman, Mullah Syed Mohammad Haqqani, as saying there was no ground fighting on Wednesday in the area, where tens of thousands of people have been displaced by heavy fighting over the past four and a half months.

Dostum leads a northern alliance fighting the purist Taleban movement, which catptured the capital Kabul last September from the forces of ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani and controls more than two-thirds of Afghanistan.
